To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PDGFRα is up-regulated in melanoma cells after BRAF-I treatment; (2) PDGFRa up-regulation is associated with BRAFI resistance; (3) PDGFRalpha up-regulation is a consequence of Shh pathway activation induced by BRAFI treatment; (4) PDGFR-alpha up-regulation is required for Shh pathway activation and for the induction of BRAFI resistance; and (5) PDGFR alpha up-regulation

PDGFRa up-regulation mediated either by PDGFRa-specific shRNA or by Shh pathway inhibitors restores and increases BRAF inhibitor (V600E) melanoma cells’ response to BRAF inhibitor in vitro and in mouse xenografts.

PDGFRalpha up-regulation is a mechanism of BRAF inhibitor resistance that is mediated by Sonic hedgehog pathway activation, and that the clinical relevance of these findings is that the combination of BRAF and PDGFRalpha inhibitors is a therapeutic option in melanoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a novel mechanism underlying the resistance to BRAF-I treatment of melanoma cells with the BRAF(V600) mutation and the identification of a therapeutic strategy to overcome this resistance.
the identification of new molecular mechanisms of resistance to BRAF inhibitors, which may lead to new therapeutic approaches in BRAF-mutated melanoma patients.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for BRAF-I resistant melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PDGFRalpha up-regulation is a mechanism that mediates BRAF-I resistance and that the inhibition of PDGFRalpha or Shh pathway can restore and increase the efficacy of BRAF-I.

PDGFRa is up-regulated in BRAFi-resistant melanomas and its inhibition restores and increases the melanoma cells’ response to BRAF-I, suggesting that the combination of PDGFRa and BRAF-I may be a promising therapeutic approach in the treatment of melanoma.
PDGFRa is a novel target for overcoming BRAF inhibitor resistance and that the PDGFRa inhibitors are potential therapeutic agents for melanoma patients with BRAF mutations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PDGFRalpha up-regulation in the setting of BRAF inhibition is mediated by Shh pathway activation, and this leads to BRAF-I resistance in melanoma.
PDGFRa is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of BRAF(V) metastatic melanomas.
we have shown that PDGFR-α up-regulation mediates the BRAF inhibitor resistance of BRAF-mutant melanoma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PDGFRalpha is an important mediator of BRAFi resistance.
PDGFRalpha up-regulation is a mechanism of BRAF-I resistance that is mediated by Shh pathway activation.
the combination of BRAF-I with PDGFRα and Shh inhibitors will be a more effective therapeutic approach than BRAF-I alone for the treatment of BRAF mutant melanoma.
